terms.gloss: private, of one person, not of the state
evidence: Caes. BG 4.1: nihil prīvātī ac sēparātī agrī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of one person, against pūblicus and commūnis (Lewis & Short): rēs prīvātae, private property (Cic. Quinct. 15); vīta prīvāta, a life away from public affairs (Cic. Sen. 22). As a noun, a private citizen (see individual).

phrases.latin: ūtiliusne sit domī atque intrā prīvātōs parietēs studentem continēre an frequentiae scholārum … trādere
phrases.english: whether it is better to keep the pupil at home, within private walls, or to hand him over to the crowd of the schools

phrases.latin: ex quō togam virīlem sūmpsit nūllō diē prius ūllam pūblicam prīvātamque rem ēgit quam in Capitōlium īret
phrases.english: from the day he came of age he never did any business, public or private, before going up to the Capitol

sources: Lewis & Short: privatus · Lewis & Short: publicus
